title: Network Delay Time
prompt:
You are given a network of `n` nodes labeled `1` to `n`. You are also given `times`, a list of directed edges where `times[i] = [ui, vi, wi]` means it takes `wi` time for a signal to travel from node `ui` to node `vi`.

We send a signal from a given node `k`. Return the minimum time it takes for all `n` nodes to receive the signal. If it is impossible for all nodes to receive the signal, return `-1`.

examples.explanation: From node 2, signals reach 1 and 3 at time 1, then 4 at time 2 (via 3). The last node to receive the signal defines the answer.
Node 2 receives the signal after 1 unit of time.

hints: This asks for the shortest path from a single source to every other node in a weighted directed graph — a classic Dijkstra setup.
Use a min-heap keyed by accumulated delay; pop the closest unvisited node, relax its outgoing edges, and repeat.
The answer is the maximum finishing time among all nodes (the slowest one to hear the signal), or -1 if any node is never reached.

solution.approach: This is single-source shortest paths on a directed, non-negatively weighted graph, which is exactly what Dijkstra's algorithm solves. Build an adjacency list, then run Dijkstra from k using a min-heap of (distance, node), always expanding the closest unfinalized node first and relaxing its edges. Once all reachable nodes have their shortest distance finalized, the answer is the maximum distance among them (the last node to hear the signal) — if fewer than n nodes were reached, return -1.
